svg.text: TOKEIRA · ARCHITECTURE
How ownership fails over
The recovery story: fencing is acquire-driven, replacement owners rebuild only what was volatile, and truth is re-read from DSQL — never from peer memory.
THE FENCE — ACQUIRE-DRIVEN, NOT CLOCK-DRIVEN
Lease expiry invalidates nothing
The epoch advances only when someone else acquires (epoch + 1 in the conditional
UPDATE) or the owner relinquishes. Until then the old owner's commits still pass the
fence — and it may quietly renew its own expired lease back. Expiry is an invitation
to take over, not an eviction.
try_acquire_bundle: INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; UPDATE … WHERE owner = old
OR owner IS NULL OR lease_expiry ≤ now → epoch = epoch + 1
The fence is checked before anything is written
Every commit reads the lease epoch and the run's expected_seq first — a stale owner gets
CommitResult::Conflict and rollback before a single row moves. Rejected renewal fences the
loser immediately; graceful relinquish bumps the epoch and nulls the owner, fencing a
drained node without waiting for any clock.
two independent rejections: the shard-epoch fence and the per-run OCC fence
caveat: single-node runs at ShardEpoch::ZERO — the check is skipped by design
A TAKEOVER, WALKED
1 · THE OWNER GOES QUIET
The renewer loops at 1s and tolerates three consecutive
errors before declaring loss; a Rejected renewal fences at
once. On loss: mark draining, purge every per-shard
tracking set — a fenced node stops scanning what it lost.
2 · THE CONTROLLER NOTICES — AND DECIDES NOTHING
Heartbeats at 5s, grace at 15s: staleness moves a node to
Unavailable and placement nominates a successor. The
controller never touches the lease — nomination is advice;
the lease row is the only truth.
3 · THE SUCCESSOR ACQUIRES
The nominated runtime calls try_acquire_bundle itself —
the conditional transaction takes the row, the epoch
advances, and from that instant the old owner's writes
die at the fence.
4 · THE SWEEP — VOLATILE STATE ONLY
Republish dispatchable WFTs, reconcile due activity
dispatches, inject due timers, rebuild the tracking sets —
all read from committed hot state. No history table is
touched; lanes hold no per-run state to rebuild. The sweep
commits nothing and is safe to run twice.
5 · NOTHING RESUMES, BECAUSE NOTHING STOPPED
The ten background loops run continuously from process
start and re-read the active-shard set every tick — a
takeover changes what they see, not whether they run.
Timers, timeouts, callbacks: covered the next tick after
the sweep marks the shard Active.
6 · THE EDGE FINDS THE NEW OWNER
Three tiers of rediscovery: drop the cached route and retry
the owner hint carried on the rejection; ask the controller
to refresh the bundle; read the lease row from DSQL
directly if the controller is unreachable. A wrong guess
costs one retry — never a wrong commit.
THE QUIET PROTECTIONS
No false timeouts at failover
The sweep restarts activity heartbeat clocks and re-anchors
schedule-to-start to the current attempt — a takeover never
times out work that was healthy on the old owner.
Delivery losses were pre-forgiven
Publish is non-fatal, eager delivery failures fall to the WFT
timeout scanner, Nexus and callbacks reconstruct from
their pending-state reads — losing memory loses nothing.
Embedded has its own clock
The control lease: 60s ownership, 20s renew, 20s admission
margin — and a deliberate 5-minute quiescence before an
expired owner's cluster may be taken over.
NOT YET WIRED — THE FLEET TRACK
The full acquire → sweep → activate unit runs today only on the embedded self-assigned shard. The controller-directive path acquires and records —
but never sweeps and never marks Active, so a directive-driven takeover currently stalls in Sweeping. Steps 3–5 above are the design; wiring them is FLEET work.
Watch it happen

tokeira_runtime_not_shard_owner_total · bundle ownership churn (controller) · lease-acquire latency via the DSQL op histogram — noting honestly: no epoch-conflict counter or scanner-lag gauge exists yet.
The invariant that survives everything:
only the holder of the current lease epoch may commit history — and the replacement owner reconstructs truth from DSQL, never from peer memory.
Companions: the authoritative runtime · server (where the fence lives) · two authorities (who nominates) · the delivery plane (what gets republished).
